R101.note: mongoose.sanitizeFilter() wraps any $-keyed nested object in $eq before the query, neutralizing operator injection from extraCriteria (matches the case's stated root cause); legitimate scalar extras still work unchanged.

R102.note: path.basename() closes the reported traversal (verified: basename('../../../etc/passwd')==='passwd'); minor unexercised residual is a bare '..' input (basename('..')==='..'), a narrow low-severity gap outside the reported attack shape.

R103.note: Switches GET to POST but never adds [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] or a global antiforgery filter, which plain MVC controllers require explicitly (not automatic like Razor Pages); explanation's claim that browsers 'do not auto-submit forms across origins' is false, so classic auto-submitting-form CSRF against the POST endpoint is still viable.

R104.note: Correctly parameterizes both uid and street via JNDI filter args ({0}/{1} mapped to param/"The streetz 4 Ms bar" in order), the standard fix for this exact OWASP Benchmark case.

R105.note: Length check boundary is exact (rejects when username_len+1+action_len>=64, i.e. when username+':'+action+NUL would exceed the 64-byte buffer) and matches the stated contract: reject oversized input, still write for inputs that fit.

R106.note: Standard mysqli prepared statement with bound parameter; preserves the null-on-failure / array-on-success contract.

R107.note: Allowlist is the only correct defense for MyBatis ${} column interpolation; whitelist matches the actual selected/sortable columns, keeps tenantId bound via #{}, and preserves the created_at default, matching the stated contract.

R108.note: Extension now derived from the content-detected MIME type instead of client-supplied originalname; MIME allowlist and accepted uploads are unchanged, only the stored extension is corrected.

R109.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES,'UTF-8') applied to both fields at HTML-construction time; correct context-appropriate encoding, no functional restriction on input.

R110.note: Bounds check exactly matches the array size (valid indices 0-7); silently discarding an out-of-range update is consistent with the function's existing void-return, silent-reject pattern for the buffer-length check.

R111.note: sendmail() closes CRLF injection (confirmed against CPython 3.13 source: putcmd() raises ValueError on \r/\n reaching mail()/rcpt()), but undisclosed behavior changes: EHLO now announces the local machine's hostname instead of the fixed 'bounce-notifier.example.com', and previously-unchecked SMTP refusals now raise uncaught exceptions instead of returning 'OK'.

R112.note: id = ANY($1) with array binding is the standard node-postgres parameterized-IN-list pattern; preserves 'return every order whose id is in ids, for any array of valid ids' contract.

R113.note: pathinfo(..., PATHINFO_EXTENSION) checks only the final extension, closing the double-extension bypass (shell.php.jpg's final extension is 'jpg', so it is now correctly rejected as not matching the double-extension trick... i.e. treated as a plain jpg name, safe from execution as PHP); legitimate multi-dot image filenames unaffected.

R114.note: reserve()->resize() fixes the reported OOB write into packet, but the stated contract explicitly requires rejecting/reporting counts larger than fields.size() instead of silent bad behavior; the fix adds no such check, so an oversized count still causes an unaddressed, undisclosed out-of-bounds read on fields.

R115.note: @Lazy self-injection routes the self-invocation through the Spring AOP proxy so the already-declared @PreAuthorize actually runs; this restores enforcement of an existing annotation rather than adding a new restriction, which is exactly what the CWE-862 finding calls for.

R116.note: Closure-based setTimeout callback avoids string-to-code evaluation entirely, passing reminderId/message as real values; also incidentally fixes prior breakage from unescaped quotes in message.
